fundamental.thesis: Deepak Fertilisers is a mid-cap ammonia-chain business. It makes industrial chemicals (nitric acid, IPA, methanol), it is a leading Indian producer of technical ammonium nitrate (TAN) for mining, and it sells crop nutrition (NPK, specialty fertilisers), with large new capacity at Gopalpur (TAN) and Dahej (nitric acid) due to start in Q2 FY27. On the official filings, FY26 revenue grew 12.0% to ₹11,506 cr, but PAT fell 21.8% to ₹739 cr. Profitability has been shrinking through the year: PAT margin slid from 8.1% (H1) to 7.0% (9M) to 6.4% (full year), and EBITDA margin from 17.3% to 14.6%. The filing-extracted trend table has no Q1 FY27 revenue or PAT, and the unverified yfinance figure (PAT ₹490 cr on ₹1,886 cr revenue) looks like it may include a one-off. Treating this as a cyclical chemicals business, we judge it on EV/EBITDA: 11.1× is about half the broad-market median (bottom 15% of the market), but it is above the 5–8× the sector card calls normal for chemical cyclicals at mid-cycle. Trailing P/E of 16.9× sits inside the 12–22× Materials range, so overall we grade it fair. The forward P/E of 10.6× and analysts raising this year's earnings estimates by 43% over 30 days already assume the new plants succeed. The biggest risks are a slow ramp-up at the new plants with debt high (debt/equity about 0.76) and free cash flow negative (−₹396 cr in H1 FY26), together with raw-material squeeze from the Middle East and a falling-margin trend.

GMDCLTD is a Gujarat state-owned miner whose main business is lignite. Mining brings in nearly all its revenue (FY26 mining revenue ₹2,508 cr out of ₹2,653 cr total), and the loss-making power segment adds the rest. In Q2FY27, revenue from the official filing rose 71.2% YoY to ₹903 cr, faster than +23.8% in Q1FY27. Reported PAT fell 63.3% to ₹171 cr, but that is because Q2FY26 included a one-time ₹474 cr GST credit; without it, PAT grew about 27%. The PAT margin is 18.9%, close to Q1's 18.0% and well below FY26's 36% (which was inflated by the one-off). The quarter was strongly cash-backed: operating cash flow was 3.9x PAT and free cash flow ₹376 cr. Because this is a capital-heavy commodity miner, the right measure is EV/EBITDA, and the reported 43.9x is far above the 5–8x mid-cycle norm for cyclicals. However, that figure, the 163% dividend yield and the 4.47 debt/equity do not fit with Q1 EBITDA of ₹267 cr and the low liabilities in the segment data, so I treat them as unreliable. On the more dependable cross-check, trailing P/E of 20.6x is at the top of the 12–22x Materials range and P/B of 2.78x with 14.2% ROE is not cheap. Forward P/E (22.0x) is above trailing, which means earnings are expected to fall, so the grade is fair, not cheap, even though the stock ranks low on P/E against the broad market. The biggest risk is that the 71% revenue jump does not match the yfinance figure (₹538 cr), and it brought only modest underlying profit growth while margins shrank.

The biggest risk is that loss-making European acquisitions and the move into an unrelated business dilute returns on capital before the core device business can absorb them, and I cannot confirm the current earnings trend without the extracted results.

fundamental.thesis: CarTrade Tech runs India's dominant online used-car marketplace across Consumer (listings), Remarketing (B2B auctions), and Classifieds (auto ads) segments, with a structurally advantaged position as organized channels continue displacing unorganised used-car trade. The single biggest risk is further deceleration in top-line growth at a premium multiple — in a RISK_OFF macro with FII selling and rising crude, any Q2FY27 revenue miss or guidance tone-shift could trigger the 25–40% de-rating the sector card explicitly flags for these names.

The Ramco Cements is a mid-sized, South India-focused cement maker. Q2FY27 profit also includes a Rs 4.8 cr exceptional gain and leaves out about Rs 8.6 cr of disputed mineral land tax, so underlying earnings are weaker than reported. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the yardstick for capital-heavy cement; my verdict is expensive. At 17.1x EV/EBITDA, 30.1x trailing P/E (above the 12–22x Materials range) and 2.6x book for only a 9% ROE, the stock is priced for a margin recovery the filings don't yet show. Forward P/E of 28.7x is barely below trailing. The broad-market peer ranks (P31 on EV/EBITDA) compare it with unrelated sectors, so I gave them little weight. The stock trades near its 52-week low, but that alone is not a reason to buy.

The main weakness is cash conversion: FY26 free cash flow was ₹-114 cr and cash from operations was only 0.48x PAT, because content-acquisition spending is running ahead of the cash it earns back.

Olectra Greentech is a midcap maker of electric buses (Mobility division, about 86% of Q1FY27 revenue, partnered with BYD) and composite polymer insulators (Energy division), which puts it at the centre of India's public-transport electrification. Earnings are also not turning into cash well: FY26 cash from operations was only 0.58x PAT and free cash flow was negative (Rs -55 cr). I graded valuation on trailing P/E because the EV/EBITDA (1066x), Debt/Equity (30.8) and Price/Sales (58x) figures in the snapshot look like data errors. At 56x trailing P/E, the stock is well above the 18-28x Auto OEM range, at the top of the 28-45x Industrials range, and in the top quarter of the broad market (P75 on P/E, P73 on P/B at 8.1x), so it is expensive. The 27.9x forward P/E assumes a sharp profit recovery that the latest quarter has not yet shown. The biggest risk is the Q2FY27 results on 9 Nov 2026: if margins keep shrinking or interest costs keep rising, a stock priced for growth could be cut down to a lower multiple.

fundamental.thesis: Hexaware is a mid-cap IT services firm reporting on a January–December year, with its strongest growth currently in Healthcare & Insurance (+31.9% YoY) and Manufacturing & Consumer (+31.1% YoY), while Travel & Transportation is shrinking (-14.5% YoY). In the latest quarter extracted from filings (Q2CY26, June quarter), revenue rose 17.9% YoY to ₹3,845 cr, but most of that came from the weaker rupee: constant-currency growth was 6.3%, up from 3.2% the quarter before. PAT fell 13% YoY to ₹330 cr, and PAT margin has slipped from 10.6% to 8.6% over the trend window, even though EBIT margin improved 352 bps YoY to 13.6%. On the IT yardstick (P/E backed by EV/EBITDA), trailing P/E is 21.8x, just under the 22–30x IT range, with forward P/E at 18.2x and EV/EBITDA at 13.0x, so I grade it fair: the discount is marginal, and sell-side FY EPS estimates have been cut 6.1% over 90 days, so the forward multiple may be too flattering. The biggest risk is that headline growth is mostly currency while PAT keeps shrinking under AI-driven pricing pressure. The September-quarter results filed on 2026-10-28 are not yet in the extracted data, so this view is one quarter stale.

fundamental.thesis: Torrent Power is a vertically integrated private utility operating licensed electricity distribution across Gujarat, Maharashtra, and UP (4.29M customers, India's lowest distribution-loss record) alongside 6.6 GW of gas, coal, and renewable generation capacity, with a further ~8.9 GWp under development including renewables, pumped storage, and coal. Q1FY27 revenue grew a modest +2.8% YoY to ₹8,124 Cr — decelerating from +10.0% in Q2FY26 and +4.3% in Q3FY26 — while Total Comprehensive Income fell 13.5% YoY to ₹639 Cr; PAT margins have contracted from ~10.5% (FY25) to ~8.3% (FY26) and an estimated ~7.9% in Q1FY27 as higher finance costs from the ₹3,632 Cr Nabha Power acquisition (June 2026, 1.4 GW supercritical coal with long-term Punjab PPAs) weigh on reported PAT despite stable EBITDA margins at ~20%. Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business (per sector card instruction), 15.03× vs a broad-market median of 23.3× places TORNTPOWER at the P25 cheapness rank; the trailing P/E of 30.25× sits above the 10–18× utility sector benchmark, but the forward P/E compressing to 23.1× signals the market is already pricing in earnings recovery from the commissioning pipeline, yielding a fair overall valuation grade. The CFO resignation (August 2026) is a governance red flag at a sensitive execution juncture for a midcap, compounded by elevated leverage from Nabha and LNG supply disruptions already suppressing thermal plant performance.

Zensar is an RPG-group mid-tier IT services firm with two businesses, Digital Services and Cloud Infrastructure, and it has a net cash position of ₹326 cr. Revenue is growing a little faster: H1FY27 revenue was ₹3,094 cr, up 10.2% YoY, compared with +7.5% to +8.7% through FY26, and Cloud Infrastructure grew 12.3%. Profit is not keeping up. H1 PAT of ₹374 cr rose only 2.7%, and PAT margin fell to 12.1% from 13.6% in FY26. Some of that drop is a one-off ₹24.9 cr Labour Code provision, but excluding it margin is still only about 12.9%. Cash conversion has also weakened, with CFO/PAT at 0.73x and only ₹22 cr of free cash flow because capex took up 8% of revenue, which is unusually high for an IT services firm. On valuation it looks cheap: trailing P/E is 12.6x against an IT sector band of 22–30x, EV/EBITDA is 8.2x (P7 across the market), and forward P/E of 11.2x is below trailing. Treat that discount with care, though. The stock is near its 52-week low, analysts have cut FY EPS estimates by about 1.2–1.4% over 90 days, and the market may be pricing in AI-driven shrinkage of mid-tier IT revenue. The feed also has several conflicting numbers: the Q1 revenue figure differs between sources, the Q2FY26 row is off by a factor of 10, and D/E of 1.68 and a 351% dividend yield contradict the net-cash position. So read the cheap grade with somewhat less confidence.

fundamental.thesis: Emami is a mid-sized Indian FMCG company selling ayurvedic personal care and healthcare brands such as Navratna, BoroPlus and Zandu, and it is now buying its way into digital-first brands (60% of IncNut Digital, majority control of Axiom Ayurveda). In H1 FY27, revenue rose +24.9% YoY to ₹2,127 cr, compared with -5.2% in H1 FY26 and -0.8% for FY26. Domestic revenue rose +31.7% while exports fell -3.9%. Much of this jump comes from the two acquisitions, and no volume growth figure was disclosed, so we cannot tell how much is real underlying demand. PAT fell -9.0% to ₹284 cr, PAT margin dropped from 18.4% to 13.1%, EBITDA margin dropped from 25.6% to 22.6%, and finance costs more than doubled to ₹11.7 cr. Yardstick: trailing P/E against the FMCG range, cross-checked with EV/EBITDA. At a 22.5× trailing P/E (18.5× forward) and 17.7× EV/EBITDA, with the stock near its 52-week low (9% of its range), it trades far below the usual 40–60× for FMCG. That looks cheap on the numbers, but the sector card warns that cheap FMCG usually points to a real problem. The biggest risk is that growth is bought rather than organic: profits are shrinking while acquisition costs rise, and analysts have cut EPS estimates by 5.2% over 90 days, which suggests the low multiple may be justified.

fundamental.thesis: Godfrey Phillips is a mid-cap cigarette-led business (Marlboro licensee, plus Four Square and Red & White) with smaller retail and confectionery arms, so it is a tobacco cash business rather than a typical FMCG name. In Q2FY27, reported revenue rose 157.2% YoY to ₹4,198 cr while PAT fell 37.7% to ₹190 cr, after a 44.3% drop in Q1FY27. PAT margin fell from about 19% in H1 FY26 to 4.5%. The revenue jump does not match the yfinance quarterly rows (₹762–1,115 cr), so it most likely reflects a change in how revenue is reported, such as duties included in the top line, rather than real demand. The falling profit is the real signal: earnings have dropped for two quarters in a row. Using P/E plus earnings direction (tobacco does not deserve the 40–65× FMCG multiple), the stock looks fair at 23.2× trailing and 20.3× forward, about 34% below the broad-market median, but that discount is offset by falling profits and weak cash conversion (CFO/PAT of 0.34x in FY26). The biggest risk is that the profit drop reflects lasting tax or volume pressure on cigarettes and keeps going.

fundamental.thesis: Bharti Hexacom is Airtel's listed subsidiary running mobile and home broadband in the Rajasthan and North-East circles, so it benefits from the same tariff increases and premium-customer push as its parent within India's three-player telecom market. In Q2FY27 revenue was ₹2,582 cr, up 11.0% YoY (Q1FY27: +10.9%, FY26: +9.4%), and PAT was ₹566 cr, up 34.0% YoY (Q1FY27: +23.2%). PAT margin rose to 21.9% from 19.2%, EBITDA margin held steady at about 55%, and mobile ARPU climbed from ₹252 (FY26) to ₹259 (Q1FY27) to ₹264 (Q2FY27). Earnings are well backed by cash: CFO/PAT was 2.05x and net debt/EBITDA is only 0.87x. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the measure the sector card uses: at 15.4x it is well above the 9–12x norm for Indian mobile operators, so the stock is expensive even though it sits near its 52-week low; trailing P/E of 41.4x is inside the 35–60x telecom band and forward P/E of 22.4x assumes further earnings growth. The main concern is that growth now comes almost entirely from higher ARPU: mobile customers fell by 16k net this quarter, churn is 2.6%, and analysts have trimmed FY EPS estimates by 2.7% over 90 days despite the strong print. That leaves the stock dependent on the next industry tariff hike, and there was also a board and management change on results day.

fundamental.thesis: UTI AMC is one of India's older mutual fund houses, with a fee-based, asset-light model and no interest-bearing debt (net cash of about ₹273 cr). It earns mainly on equity AUM and flows, and also has pension, alternatives and international arms. H1FY27 revenue grew only 1.8% YoY to ₹983 cr, while PAT rose 10.4% to ₹426 cr; the PAT gain is mostly margin, not top-line growth. The quarter split is weaker: Q2FY27 alone works out to about ₹399 cr revenue (roughly -4.5% YoY, derived as H1 minus Q1) after Q1 grew +6.7%. The domestic business grew 3.8% while the international segment shrank 27.5%, so the 'accelerating' trajectory flag reflects lumpy treasury and other income more than a real AUM-led pickup. On valuation we did not have the AUM-linked earnings yardstick an AMC should be judged on (no AUM, flow or yield data), so we fell back to P/E and EV/EBITDA. Trailing P/E is 30.5x, about 13% below the broad-market median and at the 42nd percentile; EV/EBITDA is 14.7x at the 25th percentile. With the stock near its 52-week low, this looks fair rather than clearly cheap for a slow-growing AMC. The biggest risk is that the company paid out 120% of profit as dividends and cash conversion was only 0.6x CFO/PAT in H1, which cannot last unless core fee growth picks up.

fundamental.thesis: Motilal Oswal Financial Services is a diversified capital-markets group spanning asset management, wealth, broking, housing finance and treasury, with total AUM of Rs 2.23 lakh crore (+26% YoY) and asset management now its largest profit contributor at 43% of operating PAT. H1FY27 operating PAT rose 22% YoY to Rs 1,327 cr and Q2 recurring revenue rose 27% to Rs 1,182 cr, but total PAT including treasury gains fell about 29% QoQ, from Rs 1,513 cr in Q1 to about Rs 1,070 cr in Q2; the table's 'accelerating' revenue and 'expanding' margin signals are unusable because it mixes reporting bases across periods, so no reliable multi-quarter trend or Q2 revenue growth can be stated. Using P/B against ROE, the sector card's yardstick for lenders, with AUM-linked earnings as a cross-check, the stock looks fair rather than cheap: P/B of 4.41x is rich for 15.6% TTM ROE, though it is partly supported by the 23% 10-year average ROE, 26% AUM growth and a trailing P/E of 28.85x that sits just above the 18-28x NBFC range. The biggest risk is that earnings remain tied to equity markets in a risk-off regime, with FY-EPS estimates cut 3.4% and next-FY estimates cut 4.5% over 90 days, Wealth Management PAT flat to down 2% and Capital Markets PAT down 16% in H1.

AIA Engineering makes high-chrome wear parts (grinding media, mill liners) used in mining, cement and power, and is a global leader in the segment with a net-cash balance sheet (₹406 cr net cash, debt/equity 0.13). Q2FY27 is derived by subtracting Q1 from H1. Revenue was about ₹1,113 cr, up about 6.2% YoY, slower than the +12.4% in Q1FY27, though both are better than the flat 1–3% of FY26. PAT was about ₹249 cr, down about 10% YoY, and PAT margin fell to roughly 22.4% from 29.4% five periods ago, while EBITDA margin dropped 460 bps YoY in H1 to 34.5% (from 39.1%). So volume is recovering, but the company is giving up price or absorbing cost to win it. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the yardstick for capital-intensive industrials: at 27.4x (P60 vs the broad market) and a 30.7x trailing P/E, at the low end of the 28–45x industrials range, the stock is fair, not cheap, with the price in the middle of its 52-week range. Cash conversion improved to 1.18x CFO/PAT in H1, which supports quality. But next-year EPS estimates have been cut 3.4% over the last 30 days. Some snapshot fields look unreliable and I ignored them: the 38% dividend yield, and a +55.7% upside to target that does not match the 52-week range. The main risk is that margins keep falling while the higher volumes are being won at lower prices.

The peer comparison is a broad-market fallback with no hospital peers in the set, and live data looks partly unreliable (24% dividend yield, D/E printed as 53.56), so the grade is only moderately confident. The main risk to the thesis is that profit lags revenue for longer than expected while new beds ramp up: analysts have cut FY EPS estimates by 4% over 90 days even though all 14 still rate it a buy, a common pattern before a stock re-rates lower.

fundamental.thesis: Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands is a mid-cap branded apparel company that owns Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly and Peter England, plus a smaller emerging-brands portfolio. It sells through 3,434 stores, 40,500 multi-brand outlets, 6,800 shop-in-shops, e-commerce and wholesale. In Q2FY27, revenue grew 11.0% YoY to Rs 2,266 cr, up from +3.7% in Q2FY26 and +9.6% in Q3FY26, the fourth straight quarter of double-digit growth. PAT rose 126% to Rs 53 cr, but the PAT margin is still thin at 2.3%. EBITDA margin widened 60 bps to 17.2% and same-store (LTL) retail sales grew 5.3%, the 8th positive quarter in a row, though that is slower than before. On EV/EBITDA, the right yardstick for a store-heavy retailer, the stock trades at 15.9x versus a broad-market median of 23.3x (P28), and the forward P/E of 27x is far below the sector card's 60-100x range. The trailing P/E of 58x looks expensive only because current profits are low. I grade valuation fair, and the price sitting near its 52-week low gives a reasonable entry point. The main risk is profitability: net profit is only about 2% of revenue, and debt plus lease liabilities are high, so a weak festive season or slower same-store sales could wipe out much of the profit gain.

fundamental.thesis: Brainbees (FirstCry) is India's largest multi-channel retailer for baby and kids products, with GlobalBees brand roll-ups, an international arm and preschools on the side. It is still not reliably profitable. In Q1FY27 consolidated revenue grew about 13% YoY, which management calls the best in 5 years, and India multi-channel grew 18% with same-store sales growth of 15%. Growth has been uneven rather than accelerating: +18.2% in FY25, then +11.4%, then +13.0%. Profitability is getting worse: adjusted EBITDA was flat YoY, India multi-channel EBITDA margin fell 290 bps, and the gross margin is still 260 bps short of where it was. The data for profit is unreliable: the trend table shows PAT of ₹51 cr (+34%), while yfinance shows a loss of ₹31 cr on revenue of ₹1,337 cr, and the filings index says its latest extracted results are from H1 FY26, so I am not relying on any PAT figure. The sector card says to judge loss-making platforms like this one on EV/sales, growth and unit economics, not P/E. On that basis the stock is fair rather than cheap: price/sales of 1.24x and P/B of 2.18x are low for a platform, but EV/EBITDA of 159x (most expensive in its peer set) and a forward P/E of 49x mean you are paying for a margin recovery that hasn't happened yet. The stock sits near its 52-week low, but analysts' FY estimates have been cut 15–18% over 90 days. The biggest risk is that Q2 results on 14 Nov show the promised gross-margin recovery not arriving, as quick-commerce and pharmacy competitors keep pressuring diapers (about 15% of GMV).

fundamental.thesis: Gabriel India is a domestic auto-component maker focused on shock absorbers and suspension. It leads in commercial vehicles (about 88% market share) and electric two-wheelers (about 57%), and about 40% of revenue comes from the replacement/aftermarket business. H1 FY27 revenue grew 20.8% YoY to Rs 2,673 cr, speeding up from +15.5% in Q1 FY27 and +14.8% for FY26. That leaves an implied Q2 of about Rs 1,247 cr. Profits are not keeping up: PBT grew only about 10% YoY, Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin was 8.7% against 9.6% in FY26, and the restatement after the demerger plus the new stakes in HL Mando Anand and HL Klemove make the growth partly inorganic and harder to compare year on year. Valuation is expensive however you measure it. The trailing P/E of 65x is far above the 18-28x auto band. EV/EBITDA of 36.9x (the main yardstick here, since the business is shifting toward a capital- and acquisition-heavy holding structure) and P/B of 12x sit in the top quartile of the broad market (P77 and P88). The forward P/E of 31.8x and recent FY EPS upgrades (+6.2% over 30 days) already assume strong earnings growth, while next-year estimates are edging down (-1.2% over 30 days). The biggest risk is that the deals take net debt from about Rs 2 cr to Rs 1,125 cr while operating cash flow falls 36% YoY, so any slip in integration or margins hits a stock priced for perfection.

fundamental.thesis: Patanjali Foods is India's largest edible oils company (formerly Ruchi Soya), with a fast-growing FMCG overlay spanning biscuits, nutrition, and home/personal care under the Patanjali brand — but edible oils still account for roughly 70%+ of revenues, making this a commodity-FMCG hybrid rather than a pure compounder, and that matters critically for how to frame the valuation. Q1FY27 delivered record revenue of ₹11,337 cr (+29.3% YoY, accelerating from +20.9% in Q2FY26) and PAT of ₹336 cr (+86.1% YoY), but underlying quality is deteriorating: gross margin compressed from 15.26% (Q2FY26) to 13.42% (Q1FY27), EBITDA margin fell from 6.2% to 4.8%, and PAT margin contracted to 3.0% — a persistent multi-quarter contraction signal that runs counter to the top-line acceleration. At trailing P/E 25.43×, the stock screens cheap versus the FMCG sector benchmark of 40–60×, but the discount is structurally warranted by the commodity-heavy business mix; EV/EBITDA of 25× (P55 vs broad-market peers) and P/E peer rank of P32 both point to fair value rather than genuine mispricing, and the sector card's own caution — 'cheap FMCG usually means a structural problem' — applies directly here. The overriding risk is extreme balance sheet leverage (D/E 21.3×) combined with negative FCF (CFO/PAT −1.13× in Q2FY26) — at a 5.29% US 10Y yield and with PAT margins at 3%, any commodity cost spike or interest burden increase could rapidly destroy earnings entirely.

In H1 FY27 revenue grew 36.3% YoY to ₹2,621 cr and PAT rose to ₹117 cr from ₹2 cr, with EBITDA margin up from 14.6% to 18.1%. Revenue growth has improved quarter by quarter, from -4.5% (H1 FY26) to +19.8% (Q1 FY27) to +36.3% (H1 FY27), but much of that comes off a weak base hit by a ₹42 cr provision on bad receivables, and the yfinance quarterly figures (₹734 cr in Q2) do not match the filing-based table. Because this is a capital-intensive business, I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA: 20.0x is P42 against the market and about 14% below the median, and a forward P/E of 27.7x sits at the top of the 18-28x auto-ancillary range. The 148x trailing P/E is inflated by the depressed base, so overall valuation looks fair, and with the price at the consensus target (₹697) there is little room left. The biggest weakness is cash: operating cash flow was only ₹41.5 cr in H1 (0.35x PAT) against ₹390 cr of capex, so free cash flow was -₹349 cr, inventory is building and finance costs take 4.5% of revenue. Return on equity is weak at 2.3%.

fundamental.thesis: HINDPETRO is a state-run oil marketing and refining company whose earnings depend mainly on the gap between crude costs and government-influenced retail fuel and LPG prices. Q2FY27 revenue was about ₹1,39,213 cr (H1 ₹2,84,339 cr minus Q1 ₹1,45,126 cr), up roughly 26% YoY from ₹1,10,323 cr, but this growth comes from higher prices rather than profit: Q2 PAT recovered to ₹3,625 cr (2.6% margin, partly helped by ₹3,960 cr of H1 LPG compensation) after a Q1 loss of ₹12,265 cr, leaving H1 at a ₹8,639 cr loss and H1 EBITDA margin at -1.9% versus about 6.7% a year earlier. Using P/E plus dividend yield and EV/EBITDA, the yardstick the sector card sets for OMCs, the headline 4.7x trailing P/E and 4.2x EV/EBITDA look like the cheapest in the market, but they are stale: they reflect FY26 PAT of ₹18,047 cr, while actual trailing-four-quarter PAT is only about ₹1,200 cr (roughly 70x). The 7.3x forward P/E is therefore better read as policy-priced and fair, not cheap. The biggest risk is crude above $100 with a weakening rupee: marketing losses could return while the balance sheet is already stretched, with short-term borrowings up to ₹35,933 cr, a current ratio of 0.57, negative interest coverage and an ₹18,049 cr unrecognised LPG under-recovery.

IGL is the main city gas distributor in Delhi NCR, selling CNG to vehicles and piped gas (PNG) to homes and businesses. It is still adding volume: total volumes grew 6.9% YoY to 9.86 MMSCMD in H1 FY27, CNG rose 7.5% and domestic PNG rose 11.5%. Profits, however, have collapsed. H1 FY27 revenue grew 21.4% to ₹10,654 cr, but gas purchase costs jumped 39%, EBITDA margin fell from 12% to 3%, and PAT dropped 71% to ₹211 cr (a 2.0% margin). Q2 alone was much worse: EBITDA was negative ₹31 cr and PAT was about ₹26 cr, down roughly 93% from ₹386 cr a year earlier. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA and P/E, as suits a capital-intensive utility. On those, the stock looks cheap: trailing P/E is 15.4x (inside the 10–18x utilities range), EV/EBITDA is 10.5x and the stock sits around the 12th–15th percentile of the market. But both figures are based on trailing earnings that are falling fast, and analysts have cut current-year EPS estimates by 50–59% in 90 days. So I grade it fair, and the low multiples may be a value trap. The biggest risk is that IGL cannot raise CNG and PNG prices to cover higher gas costs (in a politically sensitive Delhi market, with crude near $91 and rising), so margins stay crushed.

fundamental.thesis: Inventurus Knowledge Solutions (IKS) handles outsourced revenue-cycle management and clinical support work for US doctors and hospitals. It is a fast-growing midcap that sits between IT services and healthcare, and it is not directly exposed to the time-and-materials deflation hurting generic IT services. The latest quarter we have extracted, Q1 FY27, shows revenue of about ₹894 cr, up 20.7% YoY, and PAT of ₹194 cr, up 27.8%, for a 21.7% PAT margin. Growth is steady at around 20–21% but edging down from +21.5%, and PAT margin has slipped from 23.1% to 21.7%; FY26 revenue was ₹3,194 cr (+19.9%) with a 34.2% EBITDA margin. Valuation is fair rather than cheap. We used EV/EBITDA (25.4×) and forward P/E (25.7×) as the yardstick: both are near the broad-market medians (P57/P56), and forward P/E is well below trailing P/E (39.8×), which signals expected earnings growth. On top of that, sell-side estimates have been raised (+9% for FY27 and +18% for next year over 90 days), but P/B is high at 10.4× (P83) and the stock is at 71% of its 52-week range. The biggest open question is the TruBridge acquisition (USD 557M EV, closed July 9, 2026). It is large relative to a ₹29,200 cr company, adds a lower-margin acute-care EHR/RCM business and a lot of goodwill, and has likely raised debt. The Q2 FY27 results that first include TruBridge were filed on 2026-11-05 but are not in our extracted data, so the margin hit and leverage are still unconfirmed.

fundamental.thesis: IREDA is India's government-backed specialized NBFC for renewable energy financing, a structurally advantaged lender in the clean-energy transition with a loan book growing at ~21% annually; its PSU backing and sector tailwinds provide a durable franchise but are not substitutes for credit discipline. FY26 revenue grew 23.2% YoY to ₹8,309 cr (decelerating from 35% in FY25) while PAT grew only 10.3% to ₹1,873 cr with PAT margin contracting from 24.7% (9MFY25) to 22.5%, driven by a 227% surge in impairment provisions as Gross NPA rose sharply from 2.45% to 3.49% — the growth deceleration and credit-quality deterioration are happening simultaneously, which is the most concerning combination for a lender. Valuation: using the P/B+ROE yardstick mandated by the sector card (the primary lens for lenders), P/B of 2.28× against ROE of ~13.6% falls in fair territory; however, the peer-rank data (P16 on trailing P/E, P13 on forward P/E vs broad market) and a trailing P/E of 16.1× sitting below the NBFC sector range of 18–28× are clear cheap signals — the stock near a 52-week low at 5.6% of its 52-week range reflects the market pricing in these asset-quality concerns, not oversight. The single biggest risk is that ₹394 cr of loans artificially held in Stage II due to interim High Court orders could reclassify to Stage III NPA, compounding an already deteriorating GNPA trend and potentially triggering another provision surge that could cut PAT by a further 15–20%.

fundamental.thesis: Piramal Finance is a diversified, mid-sized NBFC focused on retail lending (housing, secured and unsecured loans) while it runs down a legacy wholesale and DHFL-era book; AUM grew about 23% YoY as of Q3 FY26. The multi-quarter trajectory is deteriorating on every dimension — revenue growth has decelerated sharply from +103.7% (FY25) through +41.7% (H1FY26) to +23.6% (Q4FY26), with Q1FY27 PAT down 34.1% YoY to ₹64 cr from ₹97 cr; PAT margins have contracted from 12.8% (Q1FY26) to 9.2% (Q4FY26), and EBITDA is also softening (₹210 cr vs ₹220 cr Q1 prior year). Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for capital-intensive Industrials (per sector card), at 17.8× vs sector median 23.3× the stock screens at P33 and appears modestly discounted, but this apparent cheapness is materially misleading — ~₹9,884 cr in contingent liabilities (₹4,306 cr EPCG customs-duty exposure + ₹5,578 cr SECI bank guarantees invoked) equate to ~64% of market cap and are absent from the EV, justifying a FAIR grade at best. Sell-side EPS estimates have been cut 43% in 90 days while all 6 analysts retain BUY — a classic pre-derating divergence — and binary resolution of the EPCG/SECI liabilities on an already-extreme D/E of 20.63× is the make-or-break risk.

EBITDA margin has slid from 19.5% (H1FY26) to 17.0% and PAT margin from 7.5% to 6.8%, so volume growth is not reaching profits. The Q2FY27 results were filed on 2026-10-24 but have not been extracted yet, and the yfinance quarterly rows (₹513 cr revenue) are clearly inconsistent with the filings and were ignored. On valuation, I used EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business: 18.8× is below the broad-market median of 23.3×, but trailing P/E of 40.8× is far above the 12–22× Materials benchmark. Forward P/E of 25.6× depends on an earnings recovery that analysts are actively cutting (FY EPS estimates down 9.3% over 90 days), so I grade it expensive, even though cement usually commands a premium and the stock sits at 13.7% of its 52-week range. 3M India is the listed Indian arm of 3M and makes diversified industrial, safety, transportation & electronics, healthcare and consumer products. It sells products rather than working through an order book, and it has net cash of about ₹420 cr. Revenue is still growing but more slowly: Q2 FY27 revenue was ₹1,452 cr, up 14.7% YoY, down from +19.0% in Q1. PAT fell 17.2% YoY to ₹158 cr as EBITDA margin compressed for a third straight period, from 20.3% in FY26 to 17.6% in Q1 and 16.1% in Q2. Management blamed a weaker rupee and higher input costs linked to the Middle East, and Q1's ₹233 cr PAT included a ₹73 cr one-off gain from a land sale. Since the business is not capital-intensive or order-book driven, I graded valuation on trailing P/E checked against EV/EBITDA: 64× P/E and 36.5× EV/EBITDA are well above the 28–45× industrials range and at P77–P96 against the broad market (P/B 20.9×). That makes it expensive even after allowing for the 42× forward P/E, the strong cash conversion (CFO/PAT 3.1×) and the expected ~₹110 cr Thermo Fisher payment. The biggest risk is that a premium-multiple stock keeps losing margin: if the rupee and input-cost pressure persist, earnings growth falls behind sales growth and the stock could lose its premium. The healthcare transition to Solventum and Thermo Fisher also clouds that segment's future revenue.

Only 145 MW is renewable, and another 4.8 GW of renewable and hydro capacity is stuck in the pipeline. In Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue grew 3.8% YoY to ₹1,956 cr and PAT rose 44.9% YoY to ₹65 cr, a thin 3.3% PAT margin. This follows a FY26 loss of ₹337 cr, which came after a ₹38,160 cr asset write-down. The 'accelerating' revenue signal is mostly noise across quarters: growth has gone +12.2%, ~+1.5%, +0.5%, +3.8%, so the real picture is low-single-digit growth with no management guidance. I used EV/EBITDA, the right measure for a capital-heavy power company, plus P/B. At 8.3x EV/EBITDA (P8 vs the broad market) and 0.69x book, the stock looks cheap. But ROE is negative at -2.1% and interest costs eat about 18% of revenue, so a large part of the discount is a fair price for balance-sheet and governance risk, not a clear mispricing. The biggest risk is group solvency: auditors have flagged going-concern doubts, subsidiary RSTEPL has defaulted on about ₹2,296 cr of debt, and lenders have called a parent guarantee of about ₹1,842 cr for SMPL, which is now in insolvency proceedings. Any of these could wipe out the equity value that the low P/B seems to offer.

fundamental.thesis: Aster DM Healthcare runs hospitals and, after the merger with Quality Care India closed on 1 July 2026, is one of India's largest hospital platforms: 38 hospitals and 10,840+ beds across 27 cities under the Aster, CARE, Evercare and KIMS brands. In Q2 FY27, its first full quarter as a merged company, revenue rose 19.0% YoY to ₹2,829 cr and normalised PAT rose 34% to ₹281 cr, a 9.9% margin. Occupancy improved 335 bps to 68%, patient volumes grew 12% and ROCE rose to 23%. This is only one clean quarter, though, and the YoY base may not be fully like-for-like after the merger, so a multi-quarter trend can't be confirmed yet. For a capital-intensive hospital business, EV/EBITDA is the right yardstick: at 45.9x the stock is about 97% above the broad-market median of 23.3x (P87). Trailing P/E of 123x is at P97, it trades at 85% of its 52-week range, and analysts cut FY EPS estimates by 8.9% in the last 30 days. Taken together, the stock looks expensive. The biggest risk is that merger integration or a slowdown in occupancy gains falls short of the growth already priced in.

fundamental.thesis: Anupam Rasayan makes custom-synthesis specialty chemicals for agrochem, pharma and personal-care customers, and has now moved into finished medicines by buying a 50.07% controlling stake in Bliss GVS Pharma. Growth is slowing fast: Q2 FY27 revenue was a record Rs 821 Cr, but that is only +11% YoY, down from +35% in Q1 FY27 and +149% in Q2 FY26. EBITDA margin improved to about 25% from 19% a year ago, but PAT margin has stayed flat at about 7.7–7.8%, which suggests interest, depreciation and minority interest are absorbing the gains. Specialty chemicals trade above commodity materials, so I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA plus P/B and ROE. On that basis the stock is expensive: EV/EBITDA is 32.6x against 5–8x for mid-cycle chemical cyclicals and 23.3x for the broad-market median (P68). Trailing P/E is 83.7x (P89), and P/B of 4.4x is backed by only 5.8% ROE. The forward P/E of 42x already assumes earnings roughly double. The biggest risk is that this optimism is not met: FY earnings estimates have been cut 22% over 90 days, free cash flow was negative in FY26 (Rs -221 Cr), and integrating Bliss GVS brings execution risk.
